interface.name: limitless_window_style_v1

description.summary: window style hints for applications

interface.description: Malaysia rounds every window it composites (ADR 0059). As in macOS Tahoe, the corner radius depends on the window's bar. A client-decorated application uses this global to say which bar its toplevel draws. It grants nothing, so every client may bind it. Without it, the compositor picks the radius from the window's decoration and role.

enum.name: bar

description.summary: kind of bar a toplevel draws

enum.description: Each value matches an AppKit window kind and its corner radius.

entry.name: titlebar
entry.summary: a plain titlebar, as NSWindow without a toolbar

entry.name: unified_compact
entry.summary: a compact toolbar, as NSWindowToolbarStyle.unifiedCompact

entry.name: unified
entry.summary: a full toolbar, as NSWindowToolbarStyle.unified

entry.name: utility
entry.summary: a panel or utility window

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the global object

request.description: Bars already set stay in place.

request.name: set_bar

description.summary: the bar the toplevel draws

request.description: Tells the compositor which bar the toplevel whose wl_surface is given draws, so its frame gets that bar's corner from the next frame on. A later request replaces it. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

request.name: set_popover

description.summary: the popup is a popover with an arrow

request.description: Tells the compositor that the xdg_popup whose wl_surface is given is a popover, as NSPopover. The arrow-height logical pixels of its window geometry along the edge that faces the popup's anchor rectangle are the arrow band: the bottom edge when the popup lies above the anchor, the right edge when it lies to its left, the left edge when it lies to its right, and the top edge otherwise. The compositor shapes the body beside that band with the popover corner, and joins to it an arrow that points at the centre of the anchor rectangle, clamped to the body. It is set_popover_shape with the popover shape. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

enum.name: panel

description.summary: how a panel behaves

enum.description: Each flag matches an AppKit NSPanel property.

entry.name: hides_on_deactivate
entry.summary: hidden while no toplevel of its client is active, as hidesOnDeactivate

entry.name: floating
entry.summary: stacked above every toplevel of its client, as isFloatingPanel

entry.name: key_only_if_needed
entry.summary: a press does not give it keyboard focus, as becomesKeyOnlyIfNeeded

request.name: set_panel

description.summary: the toplevel is a panel

request.description:
Tells the compositor that the xdg_toplevel whose wl_surface is given is a panel, as NSPanel. A panel never becomes its client's main window: while it holds keyboard focus, the client's last focused toplevel that is not a panel stays activated and remains the active window the shell shows.
With hides_on_deactivate, the compositor hides the panel while the active toplevel belongs to another client or there is none, and shows it again, at the same place and stacking, when one of its client's toplevels becomes active.
With floating, the panel stays above every toplevel of its client.
With key_only_if_needed, neither mapping nor a press on the panel moves keyboard focus to it. The client asks for focus when a press lands on a view that needs the keyboard, with an xdg_activation_v1 token made from that press.
Send it before the first commit with a buffer. A later request replaces the flags. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

request.name: set_cards

description.summary: the layer surface draws cards

request.description: Tells the compositor that the layer surface whose wl_surface is given draws cards, as macOS notifications, at these rectangles. The array holds int32 quadruples x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels. The compositor gives each card the window frame around a continuous corner of the given radius: the shadow below the surface, and the inner and outer borders above it. The client draws the card itself with that corner. A later request replaces the cards; an empty array removes them. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

request.name: set_desktop

description.summary: the background surface belongs to one desktop

request.description: Tells the compositor that the background layer surface whose wl_surface is given shows only on desktop number desktop, counted from 1 as Mission Control numbers them (Malaysia ADR 0051). Each desktop shows its own background surface on an output and, when it has none, the background surfaces that were never given a desktop. A desktop of 0 returns the surface to every desktop. It applies from the next frame and lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

request.name: set_glass

description.summary: the toplevel has glass panels

request.description:
Tells the compositor that the toplevel whose wl_surface is given has glass panels, as the sidebar of a macOS window. The array holds int32 quadruples x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels, clipped to the window geometry. At most 16 panels are kept. The compositor fills each panel with a material and draws the window frame's inner border along its edge, around a continuous corner of the given radius. The client leaves the panels transparent.
While the toplevel is active, the material is base with the chroma of the blurred wallpaper behind the panel, and the border is a line derived from the material under it: a little lighter, with more chroma and the same hue. While it is not active, the panel is solid and has no border. base and solid are 0xAARRGGBB and their alpha is ignored. base has the lightness of the application's solid window, and the dominant color when the window is tinted with an accent. solid is base with the wallpaper's tint. chroma is the share of the wallpaper's chroma the material takes, in thousandths. rim is unused: send 0.
It is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit. A later request replaces the panels; an empty array removes them. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface. The compositor ignores it from a surface that is not a toplevel of a BarrierKit client.

enum.name: popover_shape

description.summary: corner and arrow of a popover

enum.description: Each value gives a popover its corner and its arrow.

entry.name: popover
entry.summary: an NSPopover: the popover corner and arrow

entry.name: menu
entry.summary: a menu with an arrow, as a Dock menu: the menu corner and the popover arrow

entry.name: label
entry.summary: a name label, as the Dock's: the label corner and a smaller arrow

request.name: set_popover_shape

description.summary: the popup is a popover of a shape

request.description: Tells the compositor that the xdg_popup whose wl_surface is given is a popover with the given shape, laid out as set_popover describes. A later request replaces the shape. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface.

request.name: set_plates

description.summary: the layer surface has icon plates drawn as glass

request.description: Tells the compositor that the layer surface whose wl_surface is given has icons whose plates the compositor draws, as the Dock's icons in the clear style. The array holds int32 quadruples x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels. The compositor draws each plate as the glass of a card, under the surface, around a continuous corner whose radius is corner thousandths of the plate's shorter side, so plates of any size keep one shape. The client draws only the logo on top. A later request replaces the plates; an empty array removes them. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface. Only the Dock's layer surface has its plates drawn.

enum.name: knob

description.summary: the control a glass knob belongs to

enum.description: Each value gives a knob its lens. Both outlines are part of the glass.

entry.name: slider
entry.summary: a slider's knob: the Dock's lens turned outward

entry.name: switch
entry.summary: a switch's knob: its own lens, which shows what lies outside it

request.name: set_knobs

description.summary: the toplevel has glass knobs

request.description:
Tells the compositor that the toplevel whose wl_surface is given holds knobs, as a held slider or switch, and that it draws them as glass. The array holds int32 quadruples x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels, one capsule each. At most 4 knobs are kept. The compositor draws each knob above the surface, so its lens refracts the pixels the client committed there: the client draws the control without the knob and leaves its track under it. tint is 0xAARRGGBB and its alpha counts: it is laid over the refraction. A later request replaces the knobs; an empty array removes them.
It is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface. The compositor ignores it from a surface that is not a toplevel of a BarrierKit client.

description.summary: where a material takes its pixels

entry.name: behind_window
entry.summary: what lies behind the toplevel: the wallpaper and the windows below it

entry.name: within_window
entry.summary: what the surfaces of the toplevel draw below the requesting surface

enum.name: material

description.summary: how a backdrop looks

enum.description: The semantic materials of NSVisualEffectView.Material that the macOS 27.2 SDK does not deprecate, in the order of its header (AppKit.framework/Headers/NSVisualEffectView.h), then the two styles of NSGlassEffectView (NSGlassEffectView.h). The values are this protocol's own, not the SDK's raw values. What a material looks like (blur, saturation, tint, lens) belongs to the compositor, as in macOS. A value this version does not define makes the request ignored.

entry.name: titlebar
entry.summary: window titlebars

entry.name: selection
entry.summary: the selection of a table view or a menu

entry.name: popover
entry.summary: the background of popovers

entry.name: sidebar
entry.summary: the background of window sidebars

entry.name: header_view
entry.summary: in-line header and footer views

entry.name: sheet
entry.summary: the background of sheets

entry.name: window_background
entry.summary: opaque window backgrounds

entry.name: hud_window
entry.summary: the background of heads-up display windows

entry.name: full_screen_ui
entry.summary: the background of full-screen modal UI

entry.name: tool_tip
entry.summary: the background of tool tips

entry.name: content_background
entry.summary: the opaque background of content

entry.name: under_window_background
entry.summary: under window backgrounds

entry.name: under_page_background
entry.summary: behind document pages

enum.name: edge

description.summary: a side of a surface

enum.description: As SwiftUI's Edge, with physical sides: leading is the left side and trailing the right side, whatever the layout direction.

description.summary: how a scroll edge effect ends

entry.name: automatic
entry.summary: the compositor picks soft or hard

entry.name: soft
entry.summary: the blur fades to none across the depth

entry.name: hard
entry.summary: the blur is uniform across the depth and ends in an edge

request.name: set_backdrop

description.summary: the surface has a material over what lies below it

request.description:
Tells the compositor that the surface whose wl_surface is given has a material in rects. The array holds int32 quadruples x, y, width and height in surface-local logical pixels, clipped to the surface. At most 16 are kept. The compositor draws the material in each rectangle, around a continuous corner of the given radius in logical pixels, under the surface's own pixels and over the pixels that lie below. The client leaves the rectangle transparent where the material shows and draws its content over it. The compositor picks the blur radius, the saturation, the tint and the lens, and draws the material's solid under Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast. Its blur reaches the same distance in logical pixels at every output scale.
With within_window, what lies below is every surface of the toplevel's tree that is drawn before the requesting surface: its parent, the sub-surfaces placed under it and their children. The requesting surface may be a sub-surface above its parent, a sub-surface below it, or the toplevel's own surface with a sub-surface placed under it. The blur never takes pixels from another toplevel or from the wallpaper. With nothing below the surface, the request has no effect. A capture of the toplevel alone includes this material.
With behind_window, what lies below is what lies behind the toplevel, as with ext_background_effect_surface_v1.set_blur_region, with the radius, saturation and tint of the material. A capture of the toplevel alone does not include it. A surface that sends this request and set_blur_region gets this one.
It is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit. On a synchronized sub-surface it applies with its parent's commit, as its buffer does, so the material and the pixels below it change in one frame; on a desynchronized one it applies at its own commit, and a frame can show it over the pixels of the frame before or after. A later request replaces the backdrop; an empty array removes it. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface. The compositor ignores it from a surface that is not in the tree of a toplevel of a BarrierKit client.

request.name: set_scroll_edge

description.summary: the surface has a scroll edge effect

request.description:
Tells the compositor that the surface whose wl_surface is given has a scroll edge effect, as a toolbar over scrolling content. The compositor blurs what lies below the surface, as set_backdrop with within_window defines it, in a strip of depth logical pixels along edge, from the surface's own edge inward. With soft the blur fades to none across the depth. With hard it is uniform and ends in an edge. The compositor picks the radius, the saturation and the tint. The client leaves the strip transparent and draws its content over it.
It is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit, and on a sub-surface with its parent's commit, as set_backdrop does. A later request replaces the effect; a depth of 0 removes it. It lasts for the lifetime of the wl_surface. The compositor ignores it from a surface that is not in the tree of a toplevel of a BarrierKit client.
